sentences.text: 2. During the pendency of the proceedings the parties to the lis have settled the dispute amongst themselves.
The petitioners are represented by a Power of Attorney holder viz., sister of accused No.1.
The submission of the learned counsel for petitioners is that the 1st petitioner/husband is working in Qatar and cannot come down to India as he would lose huge salary.

The parties (1st petitioner and the 2nd respondent herein) have agreed for mutual divorce and have filed a record of divorce by way of Khulla before the Court at Madikeri, the relevant portion of which reads as follows:
".... .... ....
WHEREAS thereafter on 20/4/2019 on the ill advise, party of the second part wife lodged complaint against party of the first part and her parents to Madikeri Town police, who registered the same in Crime NC: 2023:KHC:20068 No.58/2019 for the offences punishable under section 498-A, r/w 34 of IPC and 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 and also filed charge sheet which is registered in C.C.No 264/2020 pending on the board of Hon'ble C.J.M at Madikeri.
In view of the criminal case there was total breakdown of the marriage between the parties.

WHEREAS the dispute came to the notice of elderly members of the community and masjid committee and they intervened in the matter and advised the parties several times but that did not serve any purpose.

The party of the second part refused to resume marital life with the party of the first part on the other hand insisted for Khulla release for consideration of Rs.1,001/- (rupees one thousand one only).

Under the circumstances parties, their respective well-wishers, family elders and community and committee members discussed and the party of the first part husband accepted the offer and released the party of the first part from his marriage bondage on 5th January 2022, by receiving the consideration of Rs.1,001/- (rupees one thousand one only) for the release."
3. The matter before this Court is not for hearing on its merits and it is for the purpose of closure of the proceedings.

In the light of the peculiar facts, though in law Power of Attorney cannot represent the accused, I deem it appropriate to accept the settlement filed through Power of Attorney holder,
in the light of the complainant/2nd respondent being present before the Court and acknowledging the settlement between the parties.

In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and the offences being the ones punishable under Sections 498A r/w Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, which are not against the State or Society, I deem it appropriate to obliterate the proceedings pending against the petitioners.

5. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
